According to the latest IDC report, although Mac shipments in the third quarter of 2026 dropped by 11%, Apple's market share actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5% as the overall market shipments fell sharply by 20.1%. Details are as follows.

Apple outperforms most of the PC market amid headwinds

IDC today released its global PC shipment report for the third quarter of 2026, noting that although Mac shipments decreased compared to the same period last year, Apple performed significantly better than the overall market.

According to IDC preliminary data, Apple shipped 5.9 million Macs in the third quarter of 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million in the same period last year.

However, the overall PC market saw an even more notable decline, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-over-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

Apple remains in fourth place, ranked behind Lenovo (leading with 14.9 million shipments and a 23.8% share), HP (10.3 million shipments, 16.5% share), and Dell (7.6 million shipments, 12.1% share).

Among the top five vendors, HP saw the largest year-over-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS recorded the smallest decline, down 8.6% year-over-year, with 5.5 million shipments and an 8.7% market share.

The IDC report states:

Looking ahead, IDC said "concerns among channels about weak demand amid high inventory and high prices could lead to promotional activities in the near term," and added that "pricing will remain at levels well above the same period last year."

The organisation also noted that the economic environment has weakened compared to the previous quarter, which may further dampen demand and "make the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and 2027 even gloomier."
